featured_techniques.technique: Repair the emotional bond through actions beyond apology (emotional reconnect strategy)

sections.description: Defines saying sorry as a process for repairing the emotional bond with customers after a mistake, and contrasts mere apology letters with actions that aim to restore the customer’s sense of being valued and connected to the brand.
sections.title: Apology as emotional connection repair

summary: In this brief clip, Jeanne Bliss reframes apologies as a strategy for repairing the emotional bond between a company and its customers after a failure. She argues that the value of an apology lies not in issuing a letter, but in actions that restore trust and bring the customer’s heart back to a state of feeling valued or “beloved.” The message emphasizes the emotional impact of mistakes and the careful work required to re-engage customers so they want to continue talking about and with the brand.
title: Saying Sorry to Customers is about Repairing the Relationship
